events.verdict: Replay review of the out of bounds called on Ball (CHA) pursuant to a coach's challenge was deemed successful. Coulibaly (WAS) initiates illegal contact to Ball's (CHA) arm before the ball goes out of bounds and the illegal contact is deemed proximate to the play.
Sarr (WAS) is moving alongside Ball's (CHA) path and the contact is incidental as the two players come together.
Carrington (WAS) legally contests Bridges' (CHA) jump shot attempt.
Sarr (WAS) has an arm positioned across Williams' (CHA) arm, but the contact during the rebound is marginal.
Coulibaly (WAS) establishes himself in a screening position in Miller's (CHA) path and absorbs the contact.
Poole (WAS) brushes Bridges' (CHA) arm and the marginal contact does not affect his shot attempt.
Williams (CHA) legally contests Poole's (WAS) jump shot attempt.

Brogdon (WAS) places a hand on Ball's (CHA) body and does not apply force as he enters his shooting motion. After the release of the shot, there appears to be slight extension but the contact is marginal and does not affect his shot attempt.

Replay review of the foul called on Carrington (WAS) pursuant to a coach's challenge was deemed successful. Although there is no illegal contact by Carrington, Sarr (WAS) is assessed the foul for extending his hands into Green (CHA) and dislodging him from his rebounding position.
Bridges (CHA) is the last player to touch the ball before it goes out of bounds.
Brogdon (WAS) gets his hand on the ball, but Diabate (CHA) quickly loses control of it. Any contact during the play is incidental.
As Miller (CHA) and Coulibaly (WAS) pursue the loose ball, Miller extends his arm and marginal contact occurs to Coulibaly's head/face area as he gains possession of the ball.

After communicating with the Replay Center, the ruling on the floor of an offensive basket interference by Sarr (WAS) is overturned. Sarr contacts the ball after it exits the imaginary cylinder above the rim.
Sarr (WAS) contests the play at the rim and any contact with Williams' (CHA) arm is marginal.

Green (CHA) contests Poole's (WAS) jump shot and the contact after the release, and follow-through, is marginal. Poole extends his leg and creates the marginal contact as both players return to the floor.
Brogdon (WAS) legally contests Miller's (CHA) jump shot attempt.
Green (CHA) reaches in and makes illegal contact to Champagnie's (WAS) arm after gains possession of the rebound.
Sarr (WAS) legally contests Bridges' (CHA) jump shot attempt.
